own_scenes.desc: Hard Wax, una tienda sin adornos abierta en 1989 en Kreuzberg, veneraba los principios de Detroit y los manifiestos que UR le mandaba por fax. Su dueño Mark Ernestus y Moritz von Oswald, percusionista del entorno de Tresor, formaron Basic Channel, que nunca se dejaba citar ni fotografiar: una reconstrucción casi total del techno y el house desde el dub jamaicano, con bajos como ondas en un estanque y bombos enterrados bajo kilómetros de gasa («Phylyps Trak», «Quadrant Dub», «Octagon»). Inspiró a Vainqueur, Porter Ricks, Monolake y muchos más; en 2008 Von Oswald «recompuso» con Carl Craig a Ravel y Músorgski para Deutsche Grammophon.

refs.q: Basic Channel’s music was a near-total reconstruction of techno and house: starting from the principles of Jamaican “dub” and working back to the four-count beat conducive to club play.
refs.para: Basic Channel’s music was a near-total reconstruction of techno and house: starting from the principles of Jamaican “dub” and working back to the four-count beat conducive to club play. Records like “Phylyps Trak,” “Quadrant Dub,” and “Octagon” (all released in 1994) incorporate basslines that sound like pond ripples and beats buried under a mile of gauze—even the ultra-distressed typography of the label art reflects a murky composition. Basic Channel’s ideas would go on to inspire the work of Vainquer, Porter Ricks, Monolake, and a host of other innovative German techno artists.
